questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bosnia and Herzegovina article.

questions.proof: The capital is Sarajevo, and other important cities are Banja Luka, Mostar, Bihać, Zenica and Tuzla.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Bosnia and Herzegovina article.

questions.proof: After a 3-year long war, part of the Yugoslav Wars, Bosnia and Herzegovina proclaimed independence as a country consisting mostly of Serbs, Croats and Bosnian Muslims.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Countries around Bosnia and Herzegovina are _____, Serbia and Montenegro.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Serbia”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bosnia and Herzegovina article.

questions.proof: Countries around Bosnia and Herzegovina are Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “From 1918 until _____, the country was a part of Yugoslavia.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Bosnia and Herzegovina article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: From 1918 until 1992, the country was a part of Yugoslavia.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Borac handball club has won seven Yugoslav Handball Championships, as well as the European Championship Cup in _____ and the International Handball Federation Cup in 1991.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Bosnia and Herzegovina article, under the heading “Sports”.

questions.proof: The Borac handball club has won seven Yugoslav Handball Championships, as well as the European Championship Cup in 1976 and the International Handball Federation Cup in 1991.
